name: Varangian Guards
headerMeta: Golden era · Melee infantry · special · 290 leadership · Seasonal (S11: Helheim)
pitch: A dual-form axe-and-shield bruiser that shields up to block, then switches to wide-arc axe swings that chain into a free passive sweep for continuous damage. It wins chokepoints and stacked fights but folds to burstier rares and cavalry it can't disengage from.

veterancy.label: Bottom line
veterancy.body: Rest of the points go mid tier and top-of-mid once it splits into two ways.

veterancy.label: Top line
veterancy.body: 5 points top; capstone unlocks 'Axes of the North' (+15% dmg to infantry, renames the unit).

battleRole.positioning: No dedicated positioning guidance from any source — treat as a flexible line/flank piece. Don't take cavalry charges head-on without disengaging or bracing first, and avoid lingering in ranged-unit range out of shield formation — tier-5 ranged can still punish careless positioning even while shielded. {2}
battleRole.formation: Default F1 (dispersed): each model auto-engages its nearest target independently, reducing exposure to ranged AoE. {2} Shield-wall: models plant and hold, generate rage while holding, and auto-reposition to face attackers from behind — unreliable against fast-closing heroes or long-range attacks, so those threats need active management. {2} Ability 1 can be layered onto either formation for extra defensive positioning. {2}
battleRole.tips: Ability chain for sustained fights: ability 1 block/bash, into ability 2's axe-spin, into the passive 'Great Sweep' area attack, then re-trigger ability 2 to refresh cooldown and sweep again — keeps the unit attacking instead of idling on cooldown. {2} Ability 1's block stance drains stamina faster ('reduced tensor'); consider burning its charge before engaging a ranged unit. {2} Triggering an ability with no enemies nearby gives a movement-speed bonus instead — useful for repositioning. {2} Axe-charge momentum/knockback on hit is rated stronger than a comparable Longsword charge. {2} Wide-arc axe swings hit an estimated 10-20 enemies per swing, making this a chokepoint specialist — alleyways, tower stairwells, corner fights. {2}

cards.name: Braced-pike units (e.g. Foederati-style)
cards.why: step into their block/brace state, then trigger ability 2 once their brace window ends to punish the recovery

controls.notes: 1 (Raging Onslaught) switches to axes. {1} X to move in, then 3 → 2 → 1, pressing V between spell steps to add one extra auto-attack — practice in custom battle to time the cancels right. {1} Vs. cavalry you can't disengage: absorb the charge in shield-wall (ideally with ability-1 block active), then use ability 2 to clean up survivors after it lands — the same absorb-then-punish sequence works against braced pikes. {2}
